column1: # Where a run's time goes: timing.sh sorts each tool call into one category here.
# One rule a line: <category> TAB <tool> TAB <text> [TAB orchestrator]. <tool> and <text>
# are regular expressions (jq's, case-insensitive); an empty field matches anything. A
# fourth field "orchestrator" makes the rule the orchestrator's only. Within a command
# the first rule that matches wins, so put narrow rules above broad ones; a command no
# rule matches is "other".
#   <tool>  the tool's name: Claude Code "Bash", "Agent", "Read"; pi "bash";
#           opencode "bash" or "shell".
#   <text>  for a shell tool, each simple command in it: the command split at ; & | and
#           newlines (not inside quotes), here-document bodies left out, and wrappers
#           ("VAR=value", time, timeout N, env, sudo, nice, command, exec, a loop's "do")
#           taken off the front; so anchor a rule with ^. For another tool, its
#           description, type, file or pattern, joined by spaces.
# A call gets one category: for a shell call running several commands, the first of
# them, in the order written, that is not git or other; else git; else other. So
# `cd x && npm test` is test and `git add . && git commit` is git.
# Categories: test, lint, build, install, ci_wait, agent_wait, review, git, user_wait,
# other. Model time (between tool calls) is not a tool call, so it has no rules; nor does
# review time, which is all of a review agent's time but its test, lint, build, install
# and CI time, nor the user_wait of an open question.md (timing.sh's header has the
# details). A dialog that asks the user is user_wait by its rule below, and is not capped
# at 30 minutes as other calls are.
# A shell call that waits on a terminal by name (`hc wait ci`) counts as what that
# terminal runs, when an earlier call started it with `hc run --name ci -- <command>` and
# <command> is test, lint, build, install or ci_wait here; so does a call that runs one in
# the foreground (`hc run -- npm test`). timing.sh does that, not a rule.
# resources.js's PROGRAMS names the same commands in the process table; keep the two alike.
# Changing this file changes every run's breakdown the next time it is read. Edit it in
# the repository and install again: an edit to the installed copy is overwritten.
agent_wait
# The orchestrator polling its agents; for another agent a sleep is other.
agent_wait
ci_wait
install
lint
test
build
git
# A dialog asking the user: Claude Code's AskUserQuestion, opencode's question.
user_wait
review
agent_wait
